tagline: A quiet, sorrow-driven curse that seeps into the world around you — subtle decay, uneasy villagers, and a ritual-based path to cleansing.

descriptionHtml: Amumu Curse adds a slow-burning affliction inspired by sorrow itself. This is not a curse that harms you outright — it lingers, changes the mood of the world, and leaves subtle signs that something is wrong.
There are no warnings, no timers, and no flashing indicators. The curse reveals itself through atmosphere, decay, and how others react to you.
💔 The Curse & Sorrow
Once afflicted, sorrow slowly builds over time. As it grows, the world begins to feel heavier in your presence. The curse does not announce itself — it simply becomes noticeable.
🌒 Environmental Decay
Sorrow affects the environment around you:

• Torches, lanterns, and fires may flicker or dim
  • The area around you feels unstable and uneasy
  • Light itself seems to struggle as sorrow deepens
👥 Villagers & Creatures
Villagers do not take damage from the curse. Instead, they react to it.

• Villagers subtly step back from cursed players
  • Their behavior reflects discomfort, not fear
Other passive creatures are not as resilient. As sorrow grows, passive mobs near you begin to take damage, as if the land itself is slowly decaying.
🩹 Bandages
Bandages offer temporary relief, slowing sorrow’s growth but never curing it. They are meant to help you endure — not escape.
Golden Bandages are rarer and more powerful. They allow the curse to be cleansed without another player present, using the same ritual process.
🕯️ The Cleansing Ritual
The curse cannot be removed casually. Cleansing requires a ritual performed under specific conditions:

• Crying Obsidian beneath the afflicted player
  • A three-block wooden altar (any wood type)
  • Candles placed at both ends of the altar
  • The ritual must occur around midnight
Normally, another player must be present to complete the ritual. Golden Bandages allow the ritual to succeed alone.
If any part of the ritual is incorrect, nothing happens. The curse remains.
